summary_html: Court issues a **protective or restraining order** to prevent contact, remove abuser, or ensure safety without removing the child. Federal law leaves implementation to states but funds protection efforts through CAPTA and IV-B.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — authorizes protective interventions and state plan requirements  
- **SSA Title IV-B** — permits funding for protective services and court interventions

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed a domestic violence protection order and remanded because the referee's findings were too conclusory to show actual or imminent domestic violence proven by a preponderance of the evidence.
key_cases.relevance: States the burden and required findings for a protective order used to remove an abuser or bar contact instead of removing the child.
key_cases.quote: a party seeking a domestic violence protection order must prove actual or imminent domestic violence by a preponderance of the evidence

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed a two-year domestic violence protection order, holding that dismissal of an earlier petition for non-appearance did not bar a second petition alleging new incidents, and that the district court's sparse findings of assault and threatening behavior were adequate to show actual or imminent domestic violence and were not clearly erroneous.
key_cases.relevance: One of the two source decisions Niska rests on: it fixes the preponderance burden, requires specific findings of actual or imminent domestic violence, and confirms that past abuse and the history of the relationship are relevant context when a protective order is used to separate the abuser rather than remove the child.
key_cases.quote: A petitioner seeking a domestic violence protection order must prove "actual or imminent domestic violence" by a preponderance of evidence.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed a two-year domestic violence protection order, holding that domestic violence may be found on actual physical harm or on the infliction of fear of imminent physical harm, but never on fear alone of harm that might occur at some indefinite future time, and that the findings here met that standard.
key_cases.relevance: The companion source decision to Hanneman, drawing the line that a protective order cannot rest on fear of some future harm, and correcting earlier opinions that had blurred 'actual' and 'imminent' — the precise defect that produced reversal in Niska.
key_cases.quote: We emphasize that when a finding of domestic violence is based solely on fear, the fear must be of imminent physical harm.

common_failures: Failure to consider less restrictive alternatives

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: The child must be released unless continued shelter care is found required; if no petition is filed within 30 days of protective custody the child must be released from shelter care (N.D. Cent. Code §§ 27-20.3-08(3), 27-20.3-10).

timeline_requirements.starts_from: Receipt of the registered-mail, return-receipt-requested notice by the Indian child's parent, Indian custodian and tribe (15 days where notice goes to the United States secretary of the interior)
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: The first hearing in the proceeding may not be held until the ten days have run; on request of the parent, Indian custodian or tribe the court shall grant a continuance of up to twenty additional days (N.D. Cent. Code § 27-19.1-03(1)).

timeline_requirements.requirement_name: Family case plan filed with juvenile court
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Commitment of the child to the human service zone by the juvenile court (N.D. Cent. Code § 27-20.3-17(1) states only "within sixty days")
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in N.D. Cent. Code § 27-20.3-17(1).
